A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FedSA-LoRA and its rsLoRA/VeRA extensions. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLUE and GSM8K experiments, matrix-similarity measurements, and analyses of heterogeneity, client counts, and LoRA ranks.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds FedDPA comparisons, CodeSearchNet results, system-efficiency measurements, and compression experiments.

M1.justification: The main FedSA-LoRA, FedSA-rsLoRA, and FedSA-VeRA procedures remain unchanged. Appendix A.7 adds an optional FetchSGD compression adaptation that approximately halves communicated A parameters, a limited procedural extension.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates GLUE language understanding and GSM8K mathematical reasoning. v3 retains these and adds CodeSearchNet, reported as a code-generation task under non-IID partitioning in Section 5.3, extending evaluation into a distinct domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds FedDPA-LoRA, FedDPA-rsLoRA, and FedDPA-VeRA to the retained standard and FFA comparisons. FedDPA was discussed but not evaluated in v1; its inclusion supplies a substantive personalized-FL comparison across all three adaptation families.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a system-efficiency protocol measuring parameters, per-round computation time, and rounds to target accuracies of 80.94% on RTE and 90.06% on QNLI. It also adds a compression condition and CodeSearchNet's referenced default non-IID partition. Existing GLUE and GSM8K training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix A.7 adds a compression experiment on RTE and QNLI testing whether reduced A communication preserves accuracy. Existing heterogeneity, client-count, rank, and matrix-similarity analyses remain. The new Figure 3 explicitly replots existing A measurements and is not a new experiment.

E5.justification: Table 1 changes from point accuracies with unspecified repetitions to per-task means and standard deviations across three runs. v3 also identifies other results as single-run, although Table 10 reports uncertainty for the compressed variant without clarifying its run count. The PDFs do not establish v1's original repetition count.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces point results with three-run summaries and adds FedDPA rows; FedSA-LoRA's reported average changes from 90.48 to 90.43, retaining its leading position. New CodeSearchNet scores are 58.34/58.57/59.66 for LoRA/FFA-LoRA/FedSA-LoRA, alongside efficiency and compression results. LoRA's QNLI Split-3 value changes from 90.69 to 90.60. GSM8K Table 9 retains v1's results, but v3's prose gives LoRA 46.23 instead of the table's 46.24.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, Theorem 1, the convergence rate, and both appendix proofs are retained. v3 clarifies the smoothness-assumption notation and adds an eigenvalue-based justification for Assumption 3. This is new mathematical reasoning, but it is invalid as written for the stated rectangular A and B matrices.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about A learning general knowledge, B learning client-specific knowledge, selective aggregation, and extensions to rsLoRA and VeRA. Explicitly labeling the method personalized FL clarifies the already-described client-specific updates without changing these core claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly connects greater heterogeneity to the need for local B personalization and discusses the tradeoff between greater per-round computation than FFA-LoRA and fewer communication rounds. Appendix A.3 adds an explanation of aggregation errors and a claimed factor-reconstruction limitation; Appendix A.7 interprets the compression results as evidence that A communication can be reduced.

D1.justification: v3 provides a code-access link, adds FedDPA learning rates to Tables 6–8, and identifies FetchSGD with approximately 50% compression. Existing model, optimizer, hardware, precision, and main hyperparameter disclosures remain. The linked code's availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v3 explicitly situates FedSA in personalized FL using Dinh and Collins, and distinguishes its asymmetry analysis from Zhu and newly cited Tian. It adds supporting intrinsic-dimension, efficiency, and compression literature and replaces the FedAvg convergence citation to Wang with Yu. The overall related-work framework remains intact.

P1.justification: The original narrative, method description, contribution list, and section order largely remain. v3 adds targeted explanations, Model Performance/System Efficiency paragraph headings, acknowledgments, and affiliation/header updates, and reorganizes appendix subsections around the relocated GSM8K example and new material.

P2.justification: v3 expands Table 1 with FedDPA rows and uncertainty notation, enlarges the hyperparameter tables, and adds efficiency/compression Tables 2 and 10. New Figure 3 shows existing A similarities on a tighter scale. The GSM8K example moves from Table 5 to appendix Table 9; existing graphics and overall visual format are retained.

improvement.justification: The personalized FedDPA comparison, three-run main results, and measured efficiency/compression tradeoffs strengthen empirical credibility beyond v1's narrower comparisons and point estimates. The net improvement is limited by the unspecified CodeSearchNet score metric, inconsistent run reporting around Table 10, and the mathematically flawed new justification of Assumption 3. These weaknesses qualify, but do not erase, the empirical gains.
